createdBy: claude-opus-5 (found while verifying ISS-054 in production, 2026-09-19)
impact:
Found by a contradiction in production data, not by reading code. At 2026-09-20T04:38:45Z the server recorded outcome=truncated with "needed ~18438 tokens" — four minutes AFTER PERSONA.md and PLAYBOOK.md on disk had already been rewritten 16k tokens smaller (mtime 04:34).

MECHANISM: sync-server.ts and server.ts both built synthInput with readPersona()/readPlaybook() BEFORE calling enqueueSynthesis(). The queue serializes synthesis per user specifically to prevent PERSONA read-modify-write races between concurrent device pushes (synthesis-queue.ts:9) — but the reads happened outside it, so a task queued behind another one carried a snapshot taken before the earlier task rewrote the files. The serialization was real; the race survived it.

WHY IT MATTERS: the observed case merely wasted a generation, because a truncated run writes nothing. A stale task that SUCCEEDS is the real hazard: it writes a PERSONA derived from pre-write state, silently discarding the newer document — exactly the corruption the queue exists to prevent.

server.ts carried a second form of the same bug: `currentPersona: persona` used a value read before the handler's own raw-observation append, so the synthesis input did not contain this session's own entries.
resolution: Both call sites now read the documents INSIDE the enqueued task, so every synthesis sees the state left by the task before it. Regression test in sync-server-synthesis-gate.test.ts holds task 1 on a gate, enqueues task 2 behind it, then releases — task 2 must observe what task 1 wrote. The test fails against the old code (sees an empty persona) and passes against the fix.
title: Synthesis inputs captured before the queue, so a serialized task can run on a stale document snapshot
